records.name: Inverness Castle
records.description: Red sandstone castle above the River Ness on the site of much older fortifications. It remains one of the defining landmarks of Inverness and a focal point for the city's evolving visitor offer.

records.name: Inverness Museum and Art Gallery
records.description: Compact museum and gallery in the city centre covering Highland history, archaeology, Jacobite stories, and changing local art exhibitions.

records.name: Inverness Cathedral
records.description: Victorian cathedral beside the River Ness known for its twin spires, peaceful interior, and strong links to the Episcopal tradition in the Highlands.

records.name: Eden Court Theatre
records.description: Major Highland arts venue presenting theatre, cinema, dance, music, and festivals on the west bank of the River Ness.

records.name: Ness Islands
records.description: Leafy chain of small islands linked by Victorian footbridges, ideal for a calm riverside walk just south of the city centre.

records.name: River Ness Walk
records.description: Scenic urban river walk passing the castle, cathedral, islands, and gardens, with some of Inverness's classic waterside views.

records.name: Victorian Market
records.description: Historic covered market hall dating from the 19th century, valued for its iron-and-glass architecture and central location near the station.

records.name: Inverness Botanic Gardens
records.description: City-run botanic garden and floral attraction with glasshouses, cactus displays, and easy access from the Bught leisure area.

records.name: Old High Church
records.description: Historic church beside the River Ness with roots in the medieval burgh and strong links to Highland religious history.

records.name: Abertarff House
records.description: One of Inverness's oldest surviving secular buildings, a 16th-century town house that preserves a rare glimpse of burgh architecture.

records.name: Inverness Town House
records.description: Prominent civic building on High Street whose ornate frontage helps define the ceremonial heart of the city centre.

records.name: Merkinch Local Nature Reserve
records.description: Coastal reserve at the Beauly Firth with saltmarsh, reedbeds, paths, and rewarding birdwatching close to central Inverness.
records.address: Near South Kessock, Inverness IV3 8AJ, Scotland

records.name: Craig Phadrig
records.description: Wooded hill topped by an Iron Age vitrified fort traditionally associated with the ancient Pictish kingdom around Inverness.

records.name: Tomnahurich Cemetery and Hill
records.description: Distinctive green hill and cemetery rising above the canal-side quarter, with wide views over Inverness and Highland hills.

records.name: Culloden Battlefield and Visitor Centre
records.description: Powerful battlefield where the 1746 Jacobite rising ended, now interpreted through memorials, grave markers, and a major visitor centre.

records.name: Clava Cairns
records.description: Exceptional Bronze Age burial cairns and standing stones, famous for their atmospheric setting and fine prehistoric stonework.
records.address: Balnuaran of Clava, Inverness IV2 5EU, Scotland

records.name: Cawdor Castle
records.description: Romantic turreted castle with medieval origins, renowned gardens, and strong literary fame through its loose Macbeth connection.

records.name: Loch Ness
records.description: World-famous deep Highland loch stretching southwest from Inverness, celebrated for dramatic scenery, boat trips, and enduring monster folklore.
records.address: Loch Ness, near Inverness IV63, Scotland

records.name: Urquhart Castle
records.description: Striking ruined castle overlooking Loch Ness, one of Scotland's most photogenic historic sites with superb waterside views.

records.name: Fort George
records.description: Immense 18th-century artillery fort on the Moray Firth, built after Culloden and notable for its scale, defences, and military museum displays.

records.name: Beauly Priory
records.description: Graceful ruined Valliscaulian priory founded in the 13th century and long associated with the Frasers of Lovat.

records.name: Fortrose Cathedral
records.description: Important medieval cathedral ruin on the Black Isle, admired for its surviving chapter house and red sandstone detail.

records.name: Chanonry Point
records.description: Narrow spit projecting into the Moray Firth, one of Scotland's best land-based spots for bottlenose dolphin watching.

records.name: Glen Ord Distillery
records.description: Historic single malt distillery near Inverness with a long whisky-making tradition and a well-known visitor experience.

records.name: Castle Stuart
records.description: Restored tower house overlooking the Moray Firth, linked to the Stuart family and dramatic coastal Highland scenery.

records.name: Moniack Castle
records.description: Historic Z-plan tower house in rural Inverness-shire, noted for its long family history and Highland setting.

records.name: Clootie Well
records.description: Traditional healing well where visitors tie cloths to nearby trees, reflecting long-surviving folk beliefs in the Highlands.

records.name: Abriachan Forest Trails
records.description: Community forest above Loch Ness with family-friendly trails, native woodland, and broad views back towards the Great Glen.

records.name: Reelig Glen
records.description: Steep wooded gorge famed for giant Douglas firs, rushing burns, and short but atmospheric walking routes.
records.address: Near Moniack Bridge, Inverness IV5 7PR, Scotland

records.name: Dores Beach
records.description: Pebbly lochside beach at the northern end of Loch Ness with excellent sunsets and expansive views down the loch.

records.name: Caledonian Canal Towpath
records.description: Easy waterside route following Thomas Telford's Caledonian Canal through Inverness, popular for walking and cycling.

records.name: Muirtown Basin
records.description: Historic canal basin where boats gather before the sea lock, offering a good sense of Inverness's maritime and engineering heritage.

records.name: Kessock Bridge Viewpoint
records.description: Viewpoint around the Beauly Firth approaches to the Kessock Bridge, with wide vistas over water, harbour traffic, and the city skyline.

records.name: Black Isle Viewpoint
records.description: Broad Highland peninsula viewpoint area valued for farmland, firth scenery, and easy day trips from Inverness.

records.name: Culloden Viaduct
records.description: Long masonry railway viaduct spanning part of the eastern Inverness landscape, best appreciated from surrounding paths and roads.

records.name: Wardlaw Mausoleum
records.description: Grand domed mausoleum of the Frasers of Lovat, notable for its Highland history, architecture, and commanding rural setting.

records.name: Kilravock Castle
records.description: Well-preserved tower castle that has remained in the same family for centuries, surrounded by gardens and wooded grounds.

records.name: Corrimony Chambered Cairn
records.description: Remarkably intact Neolithic passage grave in a quiet glen west of Loch Ness, with a striking ring of standing stones.

records.name: Glen Affric
records.description: Celebrated Highland glen of lochs, mountains, and Caledonian pinewoods, often considered one of Scotland's most beautiful landscapes.

records.name: Falls of Foyers
records.description: Dramatic wooded waterfall plunging into a gorge above Loch Ness, long admired by visitors including Robert Burns.
